_comment: One description per skill, 200 characters or fewer (the maximum the Customize → Skills
upload form documents). Since plugin 0.13.0 the SKILL.md descriptions are these same
texts, character for character (owner ruling 2026-11-12), so the plugin, both release
zips and the single-skill upload zips carry one description per skill.
scripts/build-skill-zips.py reads this file for the upload zips. This file ships in no
plugin. tests/test_skill_descriptions.py fails if a skill is missing, if a description
is over 200 characters, if a SKILL.md description differs from its entry here, or if a
description drops a trigger phrase the README advertises. Change a description in both
places, then run the trigger, non-coding and negative cases.

2026-10-28: Claude Code proxy measurement of the descriptions of that date (quiz and reference changed afterwards, in 0.12.3) vs the longer SKILL.md ones of that build on 26 routing cases x 10 runs: 259/260 vs 260/260 (CHANGELOG, 0.12.2).

0.13.0: one run per case on a build with the descriptions of that release as the SKILL.md descriptions (blindspot, brainstorm, deviation-log, interview, quiz and teach-me changed afterwards, in 0.13.3): trigger 22/22, non-coding 22/22, unknown-cell 4/4, negative cases 13/13 (CHANGELOG, 0.13.0).
blindspot: Blind-spot pass — find both sides' unknown unknowns before work on a plan or system, for an improved prompt. Use only if the user says "unknowns" or "blind spot pass" or an unknowns skill calls it.
brainstorm: Brainstorm the intervention — ~10 candidates for a named problem in any domain, today to a quarter-long bet. Use only if the user says "unknowns" or an unknowns skill calls it. NOT for design options.
buy-in: The buy-in doc — surface what approvers don't know and will object to; answer with evidence, limits and who signs. Use only if the user says "unknowns" or "buy-in doc" or an unknowns skill calls it.
deviation-log: Deviation log — log where and why the work departed from the plan, in any domain. Use only if the user says "unknowns" or "deviation log" or an unknowns skill calls it.
interview: The interview — before deciding, ask in rounds of ≤4 what you cannot know or judge in the user's situation. Use only if the user says "unknowns" or an unknowns skill calls it.
prototypes: Prototypes — several versions of anything to react to, each on a different philosophy. Use only if the user says "unknowns" or "divergent prototypes" or an unknowns skill calls it.
quiz: Comprehension quiz — explain the work, then quiz the user so they can defend it at handover; runs even when a quiz is easy to write. Use only if the user says "unknowns" or an unknowns skill calls it.
reference: Point at a reference — read an example, show your reading for correction before building on it, even when it looks simple. Use only if the user says "unknowns" or an unknowns skill calls it.
teach-me: Teach me my unknowns — an explainer for a field's vocabulary and mental model, so vague requests get precise. Use only if the user says "unknowns" or an unknowns skill calls it. Not a blind-spot pass.
tweakable-plan: The tweakable plan — decisions most likely to change come first, with alternatives, for any work. Use only if the user says "unknowns" or "tweakable plan" or an unknowns skill calls it.
unknowns-loop: Run the know-your-unknowns workflow end to end, ending with an outcome check. Use only on "unknowns loop" or "know your unknowns". A bare "loop" is NOT this.
